philosophy: The 293-season grading pass remains the source ladder; the auction-eligible pool is intentionally tighter.
Population and grading are separate decisions.
Older seasons require stronger performance or a concrete historical identity hook; recent seasons are broader but still curated.
Recognition can protect a season from the pool cut but never changes its hidden grade.
selection_order: Protect the explicitly documented identity-hook seasons.
Fill the remaining yearly slots by the already-locked hidden grade.
Do not alter grades to manufacture a target distribution.

philosophy: Grade the actual team-season, not franchise reputation.
Regular-season quality and dominance are the foundation; postseason result is meaningful but not an automatic trump card.
A dominant non-champion may grade above a weaker champion.
Recognition and historical identity affect membership only, never grade.
Final grades are curated from a reproducible baseline, then neighbor-audited.

provisional_formula.description: 76 + 32*(regular-season win rate - 0.500) + bounded scoring-margin component + postseason component; rounded to 0.5 and clamped to 74-100.
provisional_formula.scoring_margin_component: 0.5 * regular-season point differential per game, bounded from -3 to +6.

pairwise_dominance_audit.inversion_definition: Within the 200-team auction pool, a season dominates another on all three dimensions with at least one strict advantage, yet is graded more than 1.0 point lower.

runtime_note: This artifact does not change the live Weekly Auction, board generator, bankroll, roster/scoring-team count, or browser payloads. It locks the 200-team auction-eligible population and preserves the existing hidden grades for five-player market simulation. Presentation outcome labels are normalized to exact playoff exits (Lost Wild Card, Lost Divisional, Lost Conference Championship, Lost Super Bowl, Won Super Bowl, or Missed Playoffs) without changing hidden grades.
